summary: 文章讨论用机器人把小行星带到地球附近的提案，权衡近距离研究、行星防御和未来太空探索的收益。目标选择、工程可行性、安全性及高额投资，决定这些设想能否落实。
logic: 提出捕获小行星的设想

paragraphs.brief: 一个可实现的目标，而非不可能的幻想。
sentences: Send a robot into space, catch an asteroid and bring it back to Earth’s orbit.
将机器人送入太空，捕捉小行星并带回地球轨道。
This, say scientists and engineers at the California Institute of Technology (Caltech), could be feasible.
加利福尼亚理工学院的科学家和工程师可能也是可行的
A four-day workshop was dedicated to investigating the feasibility of capturing a near-Earth asteroid, bringing it closer to our planet and using it as a base for future manned space-flight missions.
一个为期四天的讲习班专门研究捕捉近地小行星的可行性，使其更接近我们的星球，并用作未来载人航天飞行任务的基础。
This is not something the scientists are imagining could be done someday in the future.
这不是科学家们想象的将来有一天可以做的事情。
It is possible with the technology we have today and could be accomplished within a decade.
有了我们今天拥有的技术，这是可能的，并且可以在十年内完成。
A robotic probe could anchor to an asteroid with simple magnets or grab it with specialised claws.
机器人探测器可以用简单的磁铁锁定小行星，或者用专门爪子抓住小行星。
Alternatively, a large spacecraft could use its gravitational field to shift the orbit of a larger asteroid, sending it towards Earth.
或者，一个大型航天器可以利用其引力场改变一个较大小行星的轨道，将其送入地球。
‘Once you get over the initial reaction — You want to do what?!
”一旦你克服了最初的反应，你想做什么？
— it actually starts to seem like a reasonable idea,’ says engineer John Brophy, who helped organise the workshop.
工程师约翰・布鲁夫帮助组织工作坊：“- 它实际上开始似乎是一个合理的想法。”
In fact, many of these ideas have been on the drawing board for years as part of NASA’s planetary-defence programme against large space-based objects that might threaten Earth.
事实上，许多这类想法多年来一直是作为美国航天局针对可能威胁地球的大型天基物体的行星防御方案的一部分而列入的。
And there’s no shortage of potential targets: NASA estimates there are 19 500 asteroids at least 100 metres wide within 45 million kilometres of Earth.
并且不缺少潜在目标：美国航天局估计，在4500万公里的地球范围内，有19,500颗小行星，至少宽100米。

paragraphs.brief: 实用、经济与科研方面的理由。
sentences: Though rearranging the heavens may seem an excessive undertaking, this US mission has its merits.
虽然重新布置天空似乎有点过分，但美国的任务有其优点。

The US already has plans to send astronauts to a near-Earth asteroid, a mission that would mean confining them in a tiny capsule for three to six months and would involve all the risks of a deep-space voyage.
美国已经计划派遣宇航员到一个近地小行星上，这一飞行任务意味着将宇航员困在一个小的太空舱里3至6个月，并涉及深空航行的所有风险。
Instead, robots could bring an asteroid close enough for them to get there in just a month.
相反，机器人可以让小行星靠近让他们在一个月内到达那里。
An asteroid would provide a stationary base from which to launch missions further into space.
一颗小行星将提供一个固定基地，从那里向空间发射飞行任务。
There are several advantages to this.
这样做有若干好处。
For one, launching missions carrying materials from Earth requires a lot of power, fuel and, consequently, money, because of our planet’s strong force of gravity.
首先，运载地球材料的发射飞行任务需要大量的动力、燃料和金钱，因为我们的地球具有强大的引力。
Since this would be far weaker on an asteroid, materials mined there could be more easily taken off the asteroid and shuttled around the solar system.
由于小行星上的这种能力会大大削弱，因此开采的材料更容易从小行星上取出，并绕着太阳系穿梭。
Many asteroids have a lot to offer.
许多小行星有很多可以提供的东西。
Some are rich in metals, which can be mined and used to build space-based habitats, or brought back to Earth.
有些金属丰富，可以开采，用来建造天基生境，或带回地球。
Others are up to one-quarter water, which could be used for life-support or broken down into hydrogen and oxygen to make fuel.
还有一些水最多为四分之一，可用于维持生命，或分解成氢和氧，以制造燃料。
Astronomers would also have the chance to get a close-up look at one of the solar system’s earliest relics, generating important scientific data.
天文学家也有机会仔细观察太阳系最早的遗迹之一，从而产生重要的科学数据。

‘Executing the asteroid-retrieval plan would help demonstrate and greatly expand mankind’s space-based engineering capabilities,’ says engineer Louis Friedman, another co-organiser of the Caltech workshop.
工程师路易斯·弗里德曼加州理工学院的另一位合作组织者：“执行小行星回收计划将有助于展示和大大扩展人类的空间工程能力。”

For instance, the mission would teach engineers how to capture an unco-operative target, which could be useful practice for planetary-defence missions in the event of a threat from a meteoroid or comet approaching our planet,’ he adds.
他又说：“例如，该飞行任务将教导工程师如何捕捉一个不合作的目标，在流星体或彗星接近我们地球时，这可能是行星防御飞行任务的有益做法。”

paragraphs.brief: 需要熟练操控并格外谨慎。
sentences: Former astronaut Rusty Schweickart, co-founder of the B612 Foundation, an organisation dedicated to protecting Earth from asteroid strikes, points out that although it would be technically feasible, shifting such a hefty and substantial target would not be easy: ‘You’re moving the largest mother-lode imaginable,’ he says.
他说：“前宇航员Rusty Schweickart是B612基金会的共同创始人，该基金会是一个致力于保护地球免遭小行星撞击的组织。他指出，尽管技术上可行，但转移这样一个巨大和巨大的目标并不容易：“你移动了最大的母地。”
Engineers would need to be absolutely certain they could control such a potentially dangerous object.
工程师们必须绝对肯定他们能够控制这样一个潜在的危险物体。

‘It’s the opposite of planetary defence; if you do something wrong you have a Tunguska event,’ says engineer Marco Tantardini from the Planetary Society, referring to the powerful 1908 explosion above a remote Russian region thought to have been caused by a meteoroid or comet.
与行星防御相反，如果你做错事了就会发生通古斯卡事件行星协会的工程师Marco Tantardini 说 1908年的爆炸发生在遥远的俄罗斯地区上空。

paragraphs.brief: 先从较容易的任务做起。
sentences: Still, these obstacles only add to the appeal of the project for engineers, who love to go over every potential difficulty in order to solve it.
然而，这些障碍只会增加工程对工程师的吸引力，他们喜欢克服所有潜在的困难，以解决这些困难。
And if the challenges posed by a large asteroid seem too daunting, researchers could always start with a smaller asteroid, perhaps two to ten metres across.
如果一个大小行星所构成的挑战看起来太可怕，研究人员总是可以从一个较小的小行星开始，可能横跨两到十米。

Last year, Brophy helped conduct a study to look at the feasibility of bringing a two-metre, 1 000-kilogram asteroid — of which there might conceivably be millions — to the International Space Station.
去年，Brophy帮助开展了一项研究，研究将一个两米、1000公斤的小行星——其中可能有数百万颗——带入国际空间站的可行性。
The study suggested the asteroid could be captured robotically in something as simple as a large bag.
研究显示小行星可以机械地在一个大袋子般简单的东西中捕捉
Of course, such a small object might not have the same emotional impact as a larger target.
当然，这样小的物体可能不会产生与更大的目标相同的情感影响。
‘NASA isn’t going to want to go to something that is smaller than our spaceships,’ says engineer Dan Mazanek from NASA’s Langley Research Center.
是美国航天局兰利研究中心的工程师丹·马扎内克：“太空总署不会想去比我们的太空船小的东西。”
No matter the size of the asteroid, these plans would require hefty investments.
无论小行星大小大小，这些计划都需要大量投资。
Even capturing a small asteroid would consume at least a billion dollars.
即使是捕捉小行星也会消耗至少10亿美元
Convincing taxpayers to foot such a bill could be difficult.
说服纳税人支付这样的帐单可能很困难。
However, private industry might be interested in getting involved.
然而，私营工业可能有兴趣参与。
One possibility would be to push the asteroid into near-Earth orbit and then invite anyone who wants to develop the capabilities to reach and mine the object.
一种可能性是将小行星推入近地轨道，然后邀请任何希望开发能力的人进入该物体并进行地雷探测。

However, although the undertaking might be scientifically exciting and provide great insight into the solar system’s formation, this is not enough on its own to justify the expense of bringing an asteroid to Earth.
然而，尽管这项工程在科学上可能令人振奋，并且为太阳系的形成提供了深刻的洞察力，但这本身并不足以证明将小行星送入地球的费用是合理的。
Investigations of asteroids can be done much more cheaply with an unmanned spacecraft, says chemist Joseph A. Nuth from NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center.
说化学家约瑟夫·A·努斯来自美国航天局的戈达德太空飞行中心：“使用无人航天器可以更廉价地对小行星进行调查。”
According to Brophy, ultimately we would be working towards bringing an asteroid closer to Earth in order to help humanity move out into the solar system.
据Brophy说，我们最终将努力使小行星靠近地球，以帮助人类进入太阳系。

items.zh: 为 A 段选择最能概括全段的标题。
items.answer: v · An achievable goal, not an impossible dream
items.solution: 一个可实现的目标，而非不可能的幻想
items.cue: 将机器人送入太空，捕捉小行星并带回地球轨道。
items.why: 研讨者认为今日技术足以尝试，并列举机器人固定或利用引力改变轨道等设想。

items.zh: 为 B 段选择最能概括全段的标题。
items.answer: viii · Practical, economic and research justifications
items.solution: 实用、经济与科研方面的理由
items.cue: 虽然重新布置天空似乎有点过分，但美国的任务有其优点。
items.why: 近地的小行星可以作基地、供水或金属，也可让研究者调查天体并验证技术。

items.zh: 为 C 段选择最能概括全段的标题。
items.answer: i · The need for skill and care
items.solution: 需要熟练操控并格外谨慎
items.cue: 他说：“前宇航员Rusty Schweickart是B612基金会的共同创始人，该基金会是一个致力于保护地球免遭小行星撞击的组织。他指出，尽管技术上可行，但转移这样一个巨大和巨大的目标并不容易：“你移动了最大的母地。”
items.why: 牵引小行星前必须能准确控制其轨道，否则本想带来的天体反而会威胁地球。

items.zh: 为 D 段选择最能概括全段的标题。
items.answer: vii · Beginning with a less challenging task
items.solution: 先从较容易的任务做起
items.cue: 如果一个大小行星所构成的挑战看起来太可怕，研究人员总是可以从一个较小的小行星开始，可能横跨两到十米。
items.why: 若大型目标难以移动，可以先捕获较小的天体，验证技术并暴露其局限。

items.zh: 为 E 段选择最能概括全段的标题。
items.answer: iv · Obtaining support for the project
items.cue: 据Brophy说，我们最终将努力使小行星靠近地球，以帮助人类进入太阳系。
items.why: 捕获项目耗资巨大，文中衡量纳税人会否买单以及私人产业有无参与动机。

需要熟练操控并格外谨慎
牵引小行星前必须能准确控制其轨道，否则本想带来的天体反而会威胁地球。
挑选矿藏最丰富的小行星
金属和水是说明项目价值的例子，文中没有按储量筛选最富的一颗。
The safest way to protect an asteroid
保护小行星最安全的方法
专家担心的是地球受到轨道失控的威胁，并非寻找保护小行星自身的办法。
捕获项目耗资巨大，文中衡量纳税人会否买单以及私人产业有无参与动机。
An achievable goal, not an impossible dream
一个可实现的目标，而非不可能的幻想

近地的小行星可以作基地、供水或金属，也可让研究者调查天体并验证技术。

items.answer: E · The skill gained could save Earth from future danger.
items.solution: 获得的技能可以拯救地球免受未来危险。

items.answer: D · An asteroid’s weight makes the project extremely challenging.
items.solution: 一颗小行星的重量使该项目极具挑战性。

items.answer: B · It might be difficult to arouse interest in an asteroid of limited size.
items.solution: 可能很难引起对体积有限的小行星的兴趣。

items.answer: A · A mistake could have serious consequences for Earth.
items.solution: 错误会给地球带来严重后果

items.en: An asteroid could also act as a ________ for further space travel and exploration.
items.zh: 小行星还可以作为________，支持更深入的太空航行与探索。
items.why: 小行星可作为进一步深空探索的“基地”。

items.en: The fact that an asteroid would have weaker ________ would allow easier movement of resources.
items.zh: 小行星的________较弱，因此资源更容易搬运。
items.why: 句子对比的是地球与小行星的引力强弱。

items.en: These resources include ________ which could be used in space or on Earth, and ____ (Q26) which could be consumed or used as a source of power.
items.zh: 可利用的资源包括能在太空或地球上使用的________，以及既可食用又可作为动力来源的________（Q26）。
items.why: 金属既能带回地球，也能在太空使用。

items.en: These resources include ____ (Q25) which could be used in space or on Earth, and ________ which could be consumed or used as a source of power.
items.zh: 可利用的资源包括能在太空或地球上使用的________（Q25），以及既可食用又可作为动力来源的________。
items.why: 水可供饮用 (消耗) 或电解成燃料。

groups.instructionsZh: 先回想空格里的英文。每空填一个词。

pairs: 原文用否定式说明移动如此沉重的目标有难度，对应题干对项目难度的描述。
题干说继续太空旅行和探索，原文写从小行星这个基地发起更深入太空的任务。
more easily taken off the asteroid and shuttled around the solar system
题干把原文的两个运输动作概括成“更容易移动资源”。
points: 研讨者认为今日技术足以尝试，并列举机器人固定或利用引力改变轨道等设想。
小行星可作为进一步深空探索的“基地”。

lead: Moving in orbit around our Sun are millions of rocks known as asteroids.
在绕太阳的轨道上移动的岩石数以百万计被称为小行星。
Now scientists have plans to capture one.
现在科学家们计划捕捉到一个
